QUESTION:
What are the most common adverse reactions to Omeprazole?

ANSWER:
The label excerpt provided does not include information about adverse reactions to this omeprazole product. However, based on standard pharmacology knowledge of omeprazole, the most common adverse reactions typically include:

• Headache (most frequent, occurring in 5-7% of patients)
• Diarrhea
• Nausea
• Abdominal pain
• Constipation
• Vomiting
• Flatulence

Less common but notable adverse reactions include:
• Dizziness
• Rash
• Elevated liver enzymes
• Hypomagnesemia (with chronic use)

Chronic use considerations:
• Long-term omeprazole use may reduce absorption of vitamin B12, calcium, and magnesium
• Risk of Clostridioides difficile infection with prolonged use
• Potential increased fracture risk with long-term therapy

For complete and accurate adverse reaction information specific to this product, you should consult the full prescribing information label or package insert. This over-the-counter product is indicated for short-term use (14-day courses), so serious adverse events would be rare at this dosing regimen. If patients experience unusual symptoms or need extended therapy beyond the labeled 14-day course, they should contact their healthcare provider.
